timeline.title: Applied Research Intern
timeline.summary: Working in an applied industrial research lab on AI agents, long-term memory, and legal technology.
highlights: Researching long-term memory functionality for AI-agentic systems in legal technology settings
Developing and evaluating agent workflows for deep legal research and long-form legal content generation
Collaborating across research, product, and engineering to prototype AI tools for legal professionals

timeline.title: Legal Intern, Capital Market
timeline.summary: Supported capital-markets matters involving IPOs, legal due diligence, and securities-law research.
highlights: Assisted the legal team in advising major corporate clients on IPOs across domestic and international exchanges
Conducted legal due diligence on corporate governance structures and material contracts to identify potential liabilities
Drafted prospectus sections and legal opinions while researching securities laws and regulatory inquiries

timeline.title: Legal Intern, Private Equity
timeline.summary: Worked on private-equity and M&A matters, including transaction documents and closing coordination.
highlights: Supported private equity funds and portfolio companies through investment and M&A transactions
Reviewed and revised Share Purchase Agreements and Shareholders' Agreements to align with client objectives
Assisted transaction closings by managing checklists, coordinating signature pages, and organizing closing binders

timeline.title: Legal Counselor
timeline.summary: Led legal support for banking transactions, cross-border financing, and institutional risk management.
highlights: Spearheaded legal negotiations for complex banking transactions with strict regulatory compliance requirements
Drafted and reviewed credit facility agreements and security documents for cross-border financing matters
Advised internal stakeholders on operational risks, dispute resolution strategy, and legal safeguards

timeline.title: Ph.D. Student in Intelligent Systems
timeline.summary: Researching AI and Law in the Intelligent Systems program under the supervision of Prof. Kevin Ashley.
highlights: Evaluating hierarchical legal reasoning capabilities in large language models
Designing trustworthy multi-agent systems for legal argument generation
Benchmarking long-context understanding and temporal logic in legal corpora
